system_prompt:
You are extracting load-bearing passages from one chapter of a guitar method book.

The user will give you the verbatim text of one chapter. Extract every passage
that does any of the following:

- teaches a technique (how to play, fingering, hand position, picking pattern)
- defines a concept (a chord type, a scale, a position system, a terminology)
- gives a rule (when to do X, what to avoid, what to prefer)
- shows a load-bearing example (an exercise that illustrates a method's
  characteristic move)

Output a JSON object with this shape:

  { "quotes": [
      { "topic": "<short topic label>",
        "verbatim_quote": "<exact substring of the input>",
        "why_load_bearing": "<one sentence on why this passage matters>",
        "page": <int, optional>
      },
      ...
  ] }

CRITICAL RULES:
1. `verbatim_quote` MUST be an EXACT substring of the input text. Do not
   paraphrase. Do not add words. Do not fix typos. Copy character-for-character.
2. If you can't find a substantial passage in the input that fits a topic,
   skip the topic — don't fabricate.
3. Skip prose that is purely biographical, motivational, or transitional.
   Keep prose that teaches.
4. Aim for 3-15 quotes per chapter. A chapter with only one load-bearing
   passage gets one quote; a dense chapter gets many.
5. `topic` is a short label (2-6 words). Use the book's own terminology
   when possible.
6. `why_load_bearing` is one sentence in YOUR voice explaining the
   significance — not a paraphrase of the quote.

          mother to take him to a guitar teacher. So he began studying guitar with José Walter, which
          gave him the first basic steps to rock and blues.

How to use this book
Although a big part of this method is exclusively dedicated to the guitar, (because it refers to
chord construction and basic visualization of the guitar fretboard),it was created as a tool for all
instruments of all levels (beginner, intermediate and advanced). However, even if you are an
advanced player, make sure you know start at the beginning of the book, otherwise you will
easily get lost by the end of the book.


This method should be used as a dictionary of ideas and techniques. It's important to understand
that the way we approach the musical concepts, ideas and techniques presented here are unique
and cannot be found elsewhere.


Do not worry about learning everything from every chapter. You can go ahead as soon as you
understand the concepts. But always remember that you can come back to any chapter of any
book in order to learn more about a determined subject you want to study again.


Be careful when trying to learn too much at one time. Music is not about quantity but quality.

    George Benson’s Picking Technique
    For many years, guitar players all over the world have been trying to understand the George
    Benson right hand picking technique. However, different from what people may think and
    unfotunately have been teaching incorrectly, both hands must work together at all times,
    otherwise nothing is going to happen.

    So do not think that it is just a matter of copying the right hand position or even the angled way
    of holding the pick, because it will not work at all. Of course the angled pick is one of the most
    outstanding features of this technique, but let's understand that although it is important, there is
    no rule about how much the pick should be angled.

    The most important thing is to remember that there is no George Benson right hand technique
    without the left hand technique (fingering). The secret is the connection between both hands.
    And yes!.. we are talking about fingering and picking choices.

    It is disappointing to know that many guitar players around the world tend to give up on this
    technique thinking they are not good enough or don't have the talent to play this way. But do not
    worry, this method was created to help you and to show you all the secrets about using this
    technique that were not available until now.
                                   68


    Although the most important thing about this technique is the connection between both hands, in
    the beginning there are some right hand exercises that will help everyone to master and
    understand this technique correctly. In the following chapters, we will start connecting both
                          46




    hands using many different melodic ideas, phrases, scales and amazing licks inspired by George
    himself.

    Let’s start splitting the picking exercises into four types:

    1) Sweep Picking

    2) “Bee” Picking

    3) Rest Stroke Picking

    4) Jumping Strings

1) Correct Fingering (digital memory)
Play the exact suggested >ingering for each melodic line or example. They were chosen
speci>ically to better help you master this technique. Study the left hand >irst, and then
after you are comfortable with the left hand >ingerings, apply the right hand.

Sometimes, the type of >ingering George Benson uses can look dif>icult because he does not
use the pinky or 4th >inger very often, playing mostly with three >ingers. But as time goes
by, it will become easier and we will be able to play much faster and more articulate than
we had ever been able to play before.

Do not forget that our >ingers have digital memory, which means that they will learn what
we teach them. If our >ingerings are inconsistent, our >ingers will not learn anything and
they will always be lost. Now, what type of connection between both hands should we
expect if one of them is totally lost? Easy answer, none !!!

3) Staccato
In order to play more rhythmic and precise, let's use a technique called staccato, which
means to mute all the notes with the left hand. In other words, we hit every note but we do
not depress the string all the way. Although it may seem very dif>icult to control in the
beginning, do not worry, the >irst step is to exaggerate the movement, thus teaching our left
hand >ingers to work together with the right hand picking.

    About the Number of Notes per String                                                         4668




    One of the most important things to correct the left hand 3ingering is the number of notes
    we play per string. The reason why it is so important is very simple: it can completely
    change the right hand picking, destroying the connection between both hands.

    A very important device concerning the "Bee" Picking Technique and the "Rest Stroke"
    Picking Technique, is that depending on the melodic line, the "down and up strokes"
    should be replaced by "up and down strokes", because everytime we want to change from
    one string to another, we should play an up stroke. So let's clarify with some examples
    below:
